records.title: Legal pack is still unsigned drafts: entity name, SCC/UK annex, insurance, governing law and two subprocessors are placeholders
records.evidenceAtHead: At 94b4f9238 every instrument is still headed as a draft: MASTER_SUBSCRIPTION_AGREEMENT.md:3 says 'DRAFT — FOR LAWYER REVIEW. NOT AN OFFER AND NOT A BINDING DOCUMENT.', and the same banner heads DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM.md:3, PILOT_AGREEMENT.md:3, ORDER_FORM.md:3 and SUPPORT_POLICY.md:3. The provider is still '[CONCEPT2CURE LEGAL ENTITY NAME]' in MSA:14, DPA:16, PILOT_AGREEMENT.md:16, ORDER_FORM.md:16 and PARTNER_HUB_APPLICATION.md:21, while the product names 'Concept2Cure, Inc.' (client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenSignup.tsx:778,854). DPA Annex III still lists '[SMTP provider — founder to name]' (:268) and '[Uptime monitoring provider — founder to name]' (:269). DPA Annex IV (:275-279) still reads 'counsel to complete'. Insurance is still a bracket in MSA §18 (:361-364) and Pilot §14 (:350-353). Governing law and venue are still '[STATE/COUNTRY]'/'[VENUE]' (MSA:368; Pilot:376-378). git diff 92ccdba1..HEAD -- docs/commercial/ shows only three changes: the DPA breach notice became a fixed 48 hours (cbed89866), the AI-subprocessor rows were rewritten so OpenAI/Vertex/Azure apply only on an Order Form election and Moonshot is removed (d29275b1b), and the onboarding runbook gained setup-token steps (b221cd641, 3b83b4a87). Entity, SCCs, insurance and counsel sign-off are untouched.
records.remaining: Everything the finding named except the 48-hour breach window and the AI-subprocessor rows. Still open: the legal entity name and jurisdiction; counsel review and sign-off; the SCC module selection and UK Addendum (DPA Annex IV), or a counsel statement that a US-only FDA pilot has no restricted transfer; the named SMTP and uptime subprocessors; insurance actually held; governing law, venue and notice addresses; and removing the DRAFT banners. Nothing in the repo shows an executed or counsel-approved instrument. A signed agreement held outside the repo would settle the pilot-level question, but none is evidenced.
records.severityRationale: A paid pilot cannot start lawfully without a signed pilot agreement and DPA. Every template in the repo is a self-declared non-binding draft that does not name the contracting entity. The defect is legal and commercial, not code, but nothing else in the catalog matters commercially until it closes.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decides the contracting entity: exact legal name, entity type, jurisdiction and registered address. Replace '[CONCEPT2CURE LEGAL ENTITY NAME]' and the adjacent '[STATE/COUNTRY] [entity type] ... [ADDRESS]' in docs/commercial/MASTER_SUBSCRIPTION_AGREEMENT.md:14, DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM.md:16, PILOT_AGREEMENT.md:16-17, ORDER_FORM.md:16 and PARTNER_HUB_APPLICATION.md:21. If the name is not 'Concept2Cure, Inc.', the product copy at client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenSignup.tsx:778,854 must change too; GTM-02 removes that inline text anyway.
2. Name the transactional-mail and uptime subprocessors in DPA Annex III (:268-269), with region and DPA reference. Use the mailer chosen under GTM-05 (one mailer). If Sentry session replay stays enabled (client/src/utils/sentry.ts), disclose it in the Sentry row (GTM-16).
3. Counsel completes DPA Annex IV (:275-279): SCC module, Annex I.A/I.B/I.C, supervisory authority and the UK Addendum tables. Alternatively, counsel states in the annex that the pilot processes data only in us-east-1 with no restricted transfer, and that the annex applies only if one occurs.
4. Fill insurance in MSA §18 (:361-364) and Pilot §14 (:350-353) with coverage actually bound (technology E&O and cyber, with limits). If none is bound, counsel decides whether to delete the section. Never state coverage that is not held.
5. Fill governing law, venue and notice addresses (MSA:368-370; Pilot:376-390) and resolve every '[Counsel: …]' note (DPA:142,189; Pilot:255,317,352,378).
6. Counsel reviews the Pilot Agreement, DPA, Order Form and Support Policy. After sign-off, replace the 'DRAFT — FOR LAWYER REVIEW' banner on each with a version line ('v1.0, approved by <counsel> on <date>'), and record the approval outside docs/evidence (a signed PDF in the company records) so that it is not only a repo claim.
7. Optional gate, kept to these documents: add scripts/ci/check-legal-pack-placeholders.mjs. It fails if PILOT_AGREEMENT.md, DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM.md, MASTER_SUBSCRIPTION_AGREEMENT.md or ORDER_FORM.md contain 'DRAFT — FOR' or any '[' placeholder outside an allowlist of deal fields ([DATE], [CUSTOMER LEGAL NAME], [CUSTOMER], [C2C-OF-YYYY-NNN], [NAME, TITLE, EMAIL], [90]). Run it at HEAD first and show it failing on the entity placeholder, then wire it into package.json as a non-blocking report until step 6 is done.
records.acceptance: (a) At HEAD, the step-7 check (or `grep -n 'LEGAL ENTITY NAME\|counsel to complete\|founder to name\|DRAFT — FOR' docs/commercial/{PILOT_AGREEMENT,DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM,MASTER_SUBSCRIPTION_AGREEMENT,ORDER_FORM}.md`) returns matches. That is the failing-first case. After the fix it returns none, and only allowlisted deal-field brackets remain. (b) DPA Annex III names every subprocessor with region and terms, and Annex IV is complete or counsel has marked it not applicable for the pilot. (c) The entity name in the templates matches any entity name shown in the product. (d) The company holds a counsel sign-off and a pilot agreement plus DPA executed by both parties. This is off-repo evidence and must be confirmed by the founder.
records.dependencies: Founder decisions (entity, domain, insurance, signatory); outside counsel; GTM-05 (which mail provider becomes the SMTP subprocessor); GTM-16 (Sentry replay disclosure).

records.title: Signup still shows non-binding inline ToS that promises HIPAA protections and a 3-month minimum; acceptance is never sent or recorded; legal URLs fall through to the app
records.evidenceAtHead:
client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenSignup.tsx at HEAD (only ddc8c0db5 touched it since the audit, and not the legal text):
- The inline ToS still says 'HIPAA protections for health data' (:801), contradicting DPA §4.1 ('does not claim HIPAA compliance', DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM.md:98-100).
- It still says 'Subscriptions require a 3-month minimum commitment' (:795), and the footer says '3-month minimum subscription' (:990).
- It still names 'Concept2Cure, Inc.' (:778,854).
- The fetch body at :299-317 sends email, password, companyName, industryMode, names, mdxSpecialization, primaryUseCases and defaultMarkets. It sends no acceptedTerms, acceptedPrivacy or aiLearningOptIn, even though those are client-side gates (:225-228, :965-966).
- The AI Model Improvement toggle (:715, :910-930) is local state only, and grep finds no server consumer of ai_learning or aiLearning.
Server side:
- signupSchema in server/routes/auth.ts:174-202 has no terms field, and nothing in server/ references acceptedTerms.
- recordAcceptance (server/services/licensing/eula-service.ts:249) is called only from POST /api/licensing/agreements/:id/accept (server/routes/licensing.ts:115), and no client code calls /api/licensing/agreements.
- requireLicenseAcceptance (server/middleware/requireLicenseAcceptance.ts:17) is defined and never mounted. It also fails open on store errors (:49-52).
- The seeded 'eula' and 'tos' rows still have no body or url (eula-service.ts:151-160).
- Both licensing tables exist only through runtime DDL in ensureSchema (eula-service.ts:109-147). They are absent from migrations/ and from C2C_MIGRATION_FILES.
Routes and links:
- client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx has no legal route. Its catch-all at :254 redirects to /concept2cure.
- The email footer links /concept2cure/legal/privacy and /concept2cure/legal/terms (server/services/emailService.ts:102-104,253-255) and the signup text cites the same URLs (ZenSignup.tsx:810,890). All of them land on the app.
records.remaining: Every element of the finding. There are no published ToS, Privacy or AUP pages. The inline copy still misstates HIPAA and the commitment term. Acceptance is neither sent nor validated nor recorded at signup. Invitees are never asked to accept. The acceptance middleware is unmounted, and it fails open. The AI-learning toggle persists nothing and contradicts the DPA's no-training position. The acceptance ledger tables are created at runtime instead of by a migration.
records.severityRationale: The pilot is sales-led under a signed pilot agreement and DPA (GTM-01), so the clickwrap is not the contract of record, which keeps this off P0. Still, the product shows every pilot user text that contradicts the DPA (HIPAA) and the paper (3-month minimum), offers a training opt-in the DPA rules out, and keeps no per-user record of acceptance. Those are misrepresentation and evidence gaps a GxP buyer's legal review will raise before production use.
records.humanTestingNote: On /concept2cure/signup the tester scrolls an inline 'Concept2Cure, Inc. — Terms of Service' that claims 'HIPAA protections for health data' and a '3-month minimum commitment', plus an 'AI Model Improvement' toggle that changes nothing. 'Full terms available at concept2cure.com/concept2cure/legal/terms' is plain text. Opening that URL, or the Terms/Privacy links in any verification or invitation email footer, redirects to the app (login or workspace) instead of a legal page. Signup still completes. Workaround: none needed to continue testing. Log these as one known legal-copy defect, not separate bugs.
records.acceptance:
Each of the following fails at HEAD first.
(1) POST /api/auth/signup without acceptedAgreements returns 400 TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED and writes no users, organizations or organization_users row. At HEAD the field is silently ignored and the account is created.
(2) A successful signup writes exactly one append-only license_acceptances row per required agreement with acceptance_hash, ip_address and user_agent, plus a chained audit row, in the signup transaction. An injected acceptance failure rolls back the whole signup.
(3) GET /concept2cure/legal/terms, /privacy and /aup render the counsel-approved text with its version and do not redirect to /concept2cure.
(4) The rendered signup page contains none of 'HIPAA protections for health data', '3-month minimum' or the AI Model Improvement toggle.
(5) With requireLicenseAcceptance mounted, an invited user with no acceptance gets 403 LICENSE_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED on a launch API and is routed to the accept page. After accepting, the same call succeeds. A licensing-store error yields 503, not access.
(6) license_agreements and license_acceptances are created by a file in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES, and eula-service.ts contains no CREATE TABLE.
records.dependencies: GTM-01 (counsel-approved ToS, Privacy Policy and AUP text and the entity name); GTM-06 (whether public self-serve signup stays open at all in production).

records.title: Member role changes and removals are now audited with a reason, cache-revoked, last-admin-guarded and operable from Admin Access
records.evidenceAtHead:
server/routes/tenant-users.ts:
- PATCH /:organizationId/:userId (:575-636) requires a reason (updateUserRoleSchema :47-50, 400 REASON_REQUIRED :55-60) and refuses self re-role (:592-594).
- In one transaction under inVerifiedOrgScope (:609-615) it runs wouldLeaveNoAdministrator and then changeMemberRole. It returns 409 LAST_ADMINISTRATOR (:617) and calls invalidateOrgMembershipCache after commit (:627).
- DELETE (:643-695) has the same reason requirement, self-removal refusal, last-admin 409 (:678) and cache invalidation (:685).
server/services/tenant/membership-change.ts:
- changeMemberRole (:80-102) locks the row FOR UPDATE, updates it and writes a sha256-chained audit row via writeChainedAuditRow carrying previousRole, newRole and reason (:48-68).
- removeMember (:144-159) records the role that was held.
- wouldLeaveNoAdministrator (:129-141) locks every admin/owner row FOR UPDATE in one order, which closes the race where two admins demote each other at once.
- A failed audit write throws and rolls the change back.
The action names member_role_changed and member_removed are read by the administrative-changes and access-review compliance reports (server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/administrative-changes.ts:66-67, access-review.ts:17).
UI: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx (:175-215) issues PATCH and DELETE with a required reason and shows the server's answer verbatim. AdminAccess.tsx:536 renders it in the member drawer.
The only other membership writers are SCIM (routes/scim.ts:416-438, audited as scim.user.deactivated) and users.ts:558, which changes the persona column only.
Ran: `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/tenant-users-audit.test.ts` → 25/25 passed. The suite covers 400 without a reason, a chained row before COMMIT, rollback on audit failure, 409 for the last admin on PATCH and DELETE, and FOR UPDATE locking.
records.fixedBy: 8167aef12 (P1-41: audited role change and removal with a reason, server/services/tenant/membership-change.ts, server/routes/tenant-users.ts); c1f2cb9ca (membership-cache revocation on commit, tenant-users.ts:627,685); ddc8c0db5 (last-administrator guard with locked admin rows, membership-change.ts:104-141, tenant-users.ts:617,678; AdminMemberActions.tsx and the AdminAccess.tsx:536 wiring)
records.severityRationale: Rated P1 at 92ccdba1. At HEAD the impact is closed: every grant change and removal leaves a chained, reasoned audit row that the access review reads, and the tenant cannot be locked out by demoting or removing its last administrator. Residual items sit outside this finding. The membership cache is revoked only on the instance that handled the request, so other instances converge within the 60s TTL (server/middleware/auth.ts:45), which is P3 at most for a single-task pilot. The over-claiming banner at AdminAccess.tsx:409 belongs to GTM-14.
records.humanTestingNote: Admin Access → member drawer: 'Change role' and 'Remove' each require a reason. Demoting or removing the only administrator is refused with 'This member is the organization's only administrator…'. The neighbouring 'Grant access', 'Audit activity', 'Edit scopes' and settings buttons still only send an AnA chat prompt, under a banner saying every action emits a Part 11 audit entry (AdminAccess.tsx:409,531-532,552,689). That is tracked as GTM-14, not this finding.

records.title: Full tenant export is still database rows only, with no stored document files; purge accepts its receipt and then deletes the tenant's vault objects
records.evidenceAtHead:
The export service has no file path:
- server/services/tenant-export/tenant-full-export.service.ts (516 lines at HEAD) discovers tables in the 'public' and 'vault' schemas (:71) and exports rows only. It never imports a storage provider and never reads object bytes. Its only sha256 is digestOf over the canonical JSON of rows (:294-296).
- recordExportReceipt (:436-491) stores digest, table_count and row_count only. The receipts table (migrations/20260813b_tenant_export_receipts.sql) has no file columns.
The route is still synchronous JSON:
- GET /api/tenant-export/full (server/routes/tenant-export.ts:172-238) builds the payload in-request and sends one JSON body.
The purge still trusts that receipt and then erases files:
- assertPurgePermitted (server/services/tenant/tenant-offboarding.ts:294-352) accepts any receipt matching the digest.
- purgeTenant (:807-870) then collects storage_version_id/storage_provider from public.purge_tenant_vault_records (:505-529; migrations/20260926_vault_documents_record_immutability.sql:195-237).
- It deletes each object through eraseStoredObjects → getStorageProviderFor(provider).delete (:622-633, :845).
There is no UI for it: no client code calls /api/tenant-export/full. The only client caller of tenant-export is the attestation (ComplianceAttestation.tsx).
The changes since the audit (66b5bb282 withholds credentials from the export; a3fbd6ff3, 7cbea4130, 2ab30c93e and c59ebc813 widen what the purge erases; 6a54db14c classifies columns) do not add files to the export or to the receipt.
records.remaining:
All of it:
- The export must include every stored object (vault uploads, rendered eCTD leaf files at server/services/ectd/rendered-leaf-files.ts:97, module attachments at server/routes/moduleIntegrationRoutes.ts:465) with a per-file SHA-256 manifest.
- It must run as an async job that survives large tenants and is delivered through a pre-signed link.
- The receipt must attest file coverage, and the purge must refuse a rows-only receipt.
- Org admins need an 'Export all data' control.
records.severityRationale: The pilot can start, and offboarding is platform-admin-only and founder-run, so it is not P0. But the first pilot that ends, or a customer exercising its data-return right, can today be purged against a receipt that never contained the customer's uploaded Vault documents. That irreversibly destroys customer files in breach of the data-return clauses. It must be fixed before pilot data is relied on in production.
records.humanTestingNote: The six launch apps do not reach it, and org admins have no export button. If a tester is given offboarding to test via the API, GET /api/tenant-export/full downloads a single JSON file with database rows only. Uploaded Vault files are missing, yet its digest still authorises a purge. Do not run a purge on any tenant whose files matter.
records.acceptance:
(1) Failing first at HEAD: a DB-tier test that seeds a tenant with Vault objects, takes the digest from GET /api/tenant-export/full and calls purgeTenant expects a refusal (EXPORT_MISSING_FILES). At HEAD the purge succeeds and deletes the objects. After the fix, it is refused.
(2) The archive job's ZIP contains every stored object for the org, and manifest.json lists each one with a sha256 that matches its bytes. An org with N stored objects yields file_count = N.
(3) If any object cannot be read, the job ends 'failed' with a message and writes no receipt.
(4) Purge succeeds only with a covers_files = true receipt whose file_count is at least the org's stored-object count at purge time.
(5) An org admin can start the export from the UI and download it through a pre-signed link that expires.
(6) A tenant of about 1 GB exports on staging with no request timeout.
records.dependencies: An S3 export prefix or bucket with KMS in the production Terraform stack. GTM-01: the data-return clause wording should cite the archive format and the link expiry once built.
